title: Audit Logging with Trigger Functions and pg_trigger_depth
realWorldScenario: For regulatory compliance, an NBFC must maintain an immutable audit trail of every update to interest rates or loan statuses, recording the old values, new values, timestamp, and the database user who executed the change.
questionStatement: Implement an automated audit trail trigger function in PostgreSQL. Detail the differences between `BEFORE` and `AFTER` triggers, statement-level vs row-level triggers (`FOR EACH ROW`), the role of `OLD` and `NEW` pseudo-records, and how to use `pg_trigger_depth()` to prevent infinite trigger loops.
expectedConcepts: FOR EACH ROW vs FOR EACH STATEMENT execution scope
OLD and NEW record structures and TG_OP variable
hints: Can an AFTER trigger modify the NEW row values?
How does to_jsonb() simplify storing arbitrary table schemas into a single audit table?
